A bachelor’s degree in any subject or a high school diploma/equivalent.
Although not required by law, The State Bar of Texas recommends completion of a paralegal or legal studies program.
At least a bachelor’s degree is required, or an associate’s degree plus experience.

No degree is currently required to operate as a paralegal in the state of NY, but the ESAPA is attempting to put through policies requiring training in a postsecondary paralegal studies program accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA).
A bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies from an American Bar Association (ABA) is advised, but there are several educational options accepted by the Keystone Alliance.

To increase the chances of finding paralegal work in Illinois, individuals should complete an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies that has been approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).
A bachelor’s degree and completion of paralegal program comprising at least 20 semester hours are required.
Although many paralegals choose a certificate program, a two or four-year degree program approved by the American Bar Association is recommended.

In order to qualify for certification, candidates will need either a bachelor’s degree from a certified program, a paralegal certificate and at least an accredited associate’s degree, or a juris doctorate.
A two-year or four-year paralegal studies degree is ideal for successful paralegal work. Students should make sure to attend a program that has been approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).

No degree is required by law to work as a paralegal, but employers will likely request a minimum education level. New Jersey colleges and universities also have a number of popular paralegal education programs accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA).
A degree is not required by law, however the VAPA recommends certain educational criteria,.
No degree is required under WA law, but an associate’s, bachelor’s or post-secondary certification program is often required by employers
To increase employment opportunities, individuals should complete either a certificate program, associate’s degree or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies.

While not mandatory, it is recommended that those pursuing paralegal careers obtain an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies from a program approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).
Before becoming a paralegal, it is a good idea to complete a two or four-year degree from a university or institution approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).
Education is key to successfully becoming a paralegal. Individuals should complete an ABA-approved paralegal studies program from an accredited institution.

The Missouri Bar Association recommends that paralegals have a minimum education of an associate’s degree in paralegal studies or have completed a paralegal certificate program that totaled 60 credit hours. However, no formal education is required.

Most employers will expect some form of post-secondary education, although it is not required by law. Maryland’s paralegal education programs do not need approval by the American Bar Association (ABA).
An associate’s or bachelor’s degree from an American Bar Association (ABA) approved program or a paralegal certificate will allow individuals to work as a Colorado paralegal.

Degrees are not required to become a paralegal in Wisconsin, although many top law firms will prefer their paralegals have at least an associate’s degree or a bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies from an American Bar Association approved program.
An associate’s degree or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies is recommended, but not required by the state of Minnesota
An associate’s or bachelor’s level degree in paralegal studies is recommended and should be earned at an institution approved by the American Bar Association.
Although no formal education is mandated, most law firms prefer their paralegals have a two or four-year paralegal studies degree from an American Bar Association (ABA) approved program.

Although it is not mandatory, candidates will be at an advantage should they choose to obtain a degree in paralegal studies. There are several programs in Kentucky approved by the American Bar Association (ABA), but ABA approval is not required.
Specialized higher education is not required, but is strongly encouraged in order to remain competitive in the applicant pool.
Completion of an authorized paralegals program of at least 60 credit hours, or a bachelor’s degree approved by the American Bar Association.
At minimum, graduation from an accredited paralegal program comprising 60 credit hours, or a bachelor’s degree in an ABA-approved program.
While there are no specific training requirements for a paralegal, most law firms will require at least an Associate’s degree.
Education is not mandated, however, the Utah Paralegal Association and the Utah State Bar Paralegal Division recommend a specialized degree.
No degree is required by Nevada, but many law firms may require an associate’s or bachelor’s to be eligible for employment
There are no mandatory education requirements for paralegals in the state. However, many law firms prefer candidates with a bachelor’s or associate’s degree in paralegal studies.
Individuals will generally need to complete a paralegal certificate program, an associate’s degree or a bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies in order to get hired by a professional law firm..

Education beyond a high school diploma is not mandatory, however many employers in the state expect candidates to have completed a program approved by the American Bar Association (ABA) or a specialized degree.
Most paralegals will complete a paralegal studies degree program that has been approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).
Holding a bachelor’s degree or an associate’s degree from a paralegal studies program can allow candidates to satisfy one of the options for eligibility.

Though not required, pursuing a degree in paralegal studies is a good idea for anyone in idea seeking employment as a paralegal. Some people in roll in certificate programs, while others pursue an associate’s or bachelor’s degree from an approved program designated by the Amer…
It is recommended, although not required, that individuals complete a paralegal studies certificate or degree from an American Bar Association (ABA) approved institution.
No minimum education level is required by WV law, but most employers expect a bachelor’s or associate’s degree in paralegal studies or a related field.
Earning a degree can make it easier to find employment. Candidates should consider enrolling in a paralegal studies degree program that has been approved by the American Bar Association (ABA).
No minimum degree is specified for paralegals under New Hampshire law, but employers may request a minimum education level or educational instruction in a certain discipline
Obtaining a degree is not mandatory, but is encouraged.
Requires an associate’s or a baccalaureate in paralegal studies from an accredited institution or a bachelor’s degree and at least 18 hours of paralegal study.

At the minimum, candidates should have a certificate in paralegal studies. However, an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies from an American Bar Association (ABA) approved institution is recommended.
A bachelor’s degree or an associate’s degree plus certificate is required in one of several state-certified fields.
An American Bar Association (ABA) approved paralegal program; an accredited paralegal program that requires 60 credit hours; a bachelor’s degree in any field.

A degree or combination of degree and certificate are required for certification in North Dakota. Paralegal programs should be 60 semester hours, or a bachelor’s degree must include 18 hours of paralegal courses.
Most Alaskan law firms will expect paralegals to possess an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies. However, this is not legally required.
A degree is not required by law, but there are certain educational standards are necessary to become a Vermont Bar Association (VBA) member.

No state requirements, but most employers prefer that candidates complete a degree or certification program approved by the ABA. This program should encompass 60 hours of paralegal-focused education. A bachelor’s degree is preferred.

Candidates with a bachelor’s degree need one year of training under the supervision of an attorney licensed with the State Board of California. High school graduates must have three years of supervised work experience. The supervising attorney must be willing to certify their …
Attorneys often prefer applicants with experience in either an educational setting or through a legal aid association.
2 years of paralegal work experience allows registration with an associate’s degree.
No minimum experience is required by the state of NY, but having experience may be a requirement for certain employers.
Between one and five years of experience depending on one's degree.

Paralegal degree programs often include a work experience segment that is completed during an internship. If the program does not include an internship, students can gain experience by working pro bono for a law firm.

2,000 hours of supervised paralegal experience are required for certification in Ohio. Alternately, 10,000 hours if applicants hold an associate’s degree or 14,000 hours (seven years) of supervised experience with no college education.
Gaining work experience after degree completion is key. Many choose to enroll in internship programs or work pro bono.
There are no experience requirements for North Carolina certification.
Law firms in Michigan will generally prefer that their paralegals have gained work experience prior to employment. Two methods for gaining experience are through an internship or pro bono work.
New Jersey does not mandate minimum experience levels, but employers may expect applicants to have experience to be competitive.
The VAPA recommends at least five years of paralegal work experience.
WA does not state a minimum experience level for paralegals, but many employers will request one year or more of experience in law

Acquiring experience by volunteering as a legal assistant or working pro bono is a requirement for most Arizona law firms. This will also help candidates develop the skills necessary for successful paralegal work.
It is a good idea to acquire paralegal experience through a degree based internship or through volunteer work before seeking employment.
Most law firms prefer that paralegals have at least some work experience. This can be acquired during the course of an internship or through volunteer legal work.
Paralegal work experience can be acquired via an internship while obtaining a degree or by volunteering at an Indiana law firm.

Paralegal studies degrees may be accompanied by an internship where students will acquire paralegal work experience. Those who do not participate in an internship can build experience through pro bono or volunteer work.
Candidates with experience are often preferred. Experience can be obtained through college internships or through the Maryland Legal Aid Bureau.

Most Colorado law firms prefer their paralegals gain experience before being employed. Experience may be gained through a degree program during an internship or via pro bono work until the candidate is ready to seek employment.
Before becoming employed, many paralegals try to acquire professional experience. The easiest ways to gain paralegal experience are in an internship or through pro bono legal work.
Work experience will make candidates more attractive to law firms. In addition, the Minnesota Paralegal Association requires experience for those seeking certification.
Aspiring paralegals should acquire work experience before seeking employment, which can be done during a degree based internship or through legal volunteering.
Before an individual can be employed in a law firm, they will often be required to gain paralegal experience either through the course of their degree program or by working pro bono.
Professional experience may be obtained through a student's college or university’s paralegal program or through Kentucky’s volunteer opportunities, such as the Legal Aid Society in Louisville.
Experience may be obtained through completion of an internship or other work opportunities in the state. It is vital to have some experience to increase the chances of being hired.

While experience is not strictly required, it can offset some of the degree requirements and paralegals must work under the supervision of a licensed attorney who assumes responsibility for their work.
Five years of supervised experience can substitute for formal education.
While there’s no experience requirement, more experience increases the odds of landing a good job.

Internships are often part of American Board Association (ABA)-approved paralegal studies programs. Additionally, there are numerous pro bono work experience options in the state. Experience is not required, but is strongly recommended in order to be considered for a position.
Nevada has no minimum experience requirement, but many law firms may require one or more years of experience in a legal setting
The right experience can be a huge advantage for paralegal job applicants. This may be achieved through educational programs and internships or through volunteering at a pro bono organization.

Many paralegal degree or certification programs will feature a work experience component that will help individuals learn how to work successfully as a paralegal. Some paralegals also choose to volunteer or do pro bono work to gain experience.
Some schools require students to participate in an internship. Pro bono volunteer work is also a valid option for acquiring experience.

Because there are no requirements to be a paralegal in Mississippi, many law firms offer on the job training. It is also possible to gain work experience during an internship or through pro bono work.

In lieu of or in addition to training in a paralegal studies degree or certification program, candidates may be required to have one to seven years of “substantive law-related experience under the supervision of a licensed attorney.”
Many degree programs feature an internship component where students can achieve real-world paralegal experience. It is also possible to volunteer at a law firm to gain work experience.

Some law firms offer on the job training for paralegals. It is also possible to participate in a paralegal internship while obtaining a degree, or to volunteer to work in a law firm. Work experience is useful when seeking employment.
WV does not mandate minimum experience levels, but many employers may expect all applicants to have one or more years of relevant experience.

Many Hawaii law firms will offer on-the-job paralegal training. However, individuals may also gain experience while obtaining their degree, which may contain an internship, or by volunteering with a law firm.
No experience is required by New Hampshire law, but experience can be a minimum requirement or a competitive advantage when applying for paralegal positions

Many employers will not consider applicants without experience or training in the field. Candidates may gain valuable experience through internships offered through Maine’s schools or by volunteering at a legal aid organization.
Individuals with only a high school diploma need 4,800 hours of legal work experience under an attorney’s supervision and 5 continuing education hours focused on legal ethics.
Work experience is recommended. While many paralegal degree programs offer internships, applicants can also gain experience through volunteer work.
Four or five years of experience can substitute for some or all of the educational requirements.
Depending on one's education, individuals may be required to gain three years of legal experience and up to two years of in-house paralegal training.
1 year of on-the-job training can substitute for a portion of the education requirements. 7 years of experience as a paralegal supervised by a lawyer can replace educational requirements.
Gaining experience will make it easier for paralegals to find employment. Many degree or certificate programs include an internship component where participants can acquire experience.
It is recommended that candidates have first-hand experience either through an internship or through a legal aid or pro bono organization.
No experience is necessary, but if seeking national certification, it can sometimes substitute for partial education requirements.

Individuals certified with the Keystone Alliance must follow ethical guidelines that have been established for membership in the organization.
Paralegals usually will need training in legal ethics and then should abide by the ethical standards of their profession.
Many professional paralegal organization maintain ethical guidelines that members must follow.
Paralegal ethical standards should be followed throughout one's career.
Must be supervised by a licensed attorney
Paralegals in the state of Connecticut must work under the supervision of a state-licensed lawyer.
Paralegals who are members of paralegal organization must follow any ethical rules for the paralegal profession.
A paralegal must have the education or experience necessary to perform legal functions and work under the supervision of an attorney or corporation.
As with all legal professionals, paralegals must follow proper ethics.

Paralegals in California must complete eight hours of continuing education every two years. Four hours should be dedicated to ethics and four hours should either be in general law or a specific legal field.
